summary: Selection sort repeatedly finds the smallest unsorted value and swaps it into place. Insertion sort takes each value and shifts larger values right until it fits.
notes: items[i], items[smallest] = items[smallest], items[i] swaps two values without a temporary variable.
The outer loop of selection sort runs len(items) - 1 times. The last value is already in place.
Both functions change the list in place. They do not make a new list.
pitfall: In insertion sort, writing items[j] = current instead of items[j + 1] = current after the while loop puts the value one spot too far left and can raise IndexError or overwrite data.
